title: Microresponse SDK Handshake Conductor - PRD Scratch
content:
Purpose
This doc captures an early PRD sketch for a 'Handshake Conductor' layer in the Hosted API SDK that coordinates microresponses (tiny incremental frames), typed tool invocations, and resumable client-side checkpoints. The goal: give app engineers expressive, low-latency primitives to build multi-tool flows without leaking server-side complexity into client code.

Context and motivation
- We keep hearing from customers that tool-calling ergonomics + streaming partial outputs is the hardest part of adoption. They need: deterministic commit semantics for tool outputs, cheap resumability across flaky mobile networks, and an SDK that avoids callback hell.
- Existing hosted SDK patterns (current prototypes) provide streaming frames and tool events, but client authors end up juggling relative sequence numbers, local merge heuristics, and ad-hoc backpressure.
- The Handshake Conductor is an SDK-layer coordinator to: negotiate frame semantics with the server, manage idempotent tool-call tokens, provide a small typed runtime for partial structured responses, and present a concise async API surface to app developers.

Non-goals
- Not a full rewrite of the protocol. We keep the existing transport (http/2 + websocket fallback) and frame envelope.
- Not an attempt to standardize tool contracts across customers. The Conductor provides hooks and validation helpers, not a canned DSL for all tools.

User stories
- Mobile chat app: Developer wants to stream partial answer chunks while a background OCR tool extracts citations. If the device loses network, the app resumes from last committed checkpoint and the tool invocation is replay-safe.
- Search assistant: Server suggests reranking tools; client needs to display progressive candidate lists and cancel low-confidence tool work when latency budget is exceeded.
- Enterprise automation: Customers want audit-ids and committed tool outputs persisted for compliance; they should be able to pin commit policy per-route.

Key concepts
- Microresponse: minimal incremental payloads (text deltas, JSON patches, typed events). Microresponses are the primary unit for incremental UX.
- Checkpoint (client-visible): a lightweight durable marker; when a checkpoint is acknowledged by the server, downstream tool outputs tied to that checkpoint are considered committed. Checkpoints survive client reconnects.
- Tool token: server-issued idempotency token for a tool invocation. The Conductor manages token lifecycle and automatic retries within policy.
- Conductor policy: per-invocation config (latency_budget_ms, commit_mode {auto|manual|deferred}, max_retries, preemptive_cancel_threshold).

Developer API (sketch)
Note: this is an SDK-level sketch aimed at JS/TS and small parity to mobile SDKs.
- conductor.startSession(route, initialContext, policy) -> SessionHandle
- session.on('microresponse', (frame) => { /* typed frame: textDelta | jsonPatch | toolEvent */ })
- session.checkpoint(label?) -> Promise<CheckpointAck>  // await acknowledgement from server
- session.invokeTool(name, args, opts?) -> ToolResultStream
  - ToolResultStream: async iterator of microresponses, exposes .cancel(), .on('meta', ...)
- session.withLatencyBudget(ms, callback) -> aborts tool work past threshold and emits 'budget:exceeded' event
- session.resumeFrom(checkpointId) -> picks up outstanding tool streams, reconciles local state with server

Behavioral expectations
- Checkpoints are cheap and frequent; most clients will call checkpoint() at natural UX boundaries (e.g., end of a paragraph).
- The Conductor will persist minimal local state (checkpoint ids, outstanding tool tokens) to indexedDB / local storage for browser SDK and secure store on mobile.
- On reconnect, SDK fetches server checkpoint map and resumes only uncommitted tool invocations. Replayed invocations reuse tool tokens to preserve idempotency.
- If commit_mode=deferred, session will batch checkpoint acknowledgements to improve throughput; policy controls max_unacked_checkpoints.

Server-side contract (summary)
- Server will return microresponse frames with fields: seq, checkpoint_hint, frame_type, payload, tool_token?  (we'll formalize schema in protocol PR)
- Server must honor tool_token idempotency and accept replayed requests that reuse token with same args.

Latency and cost model
- Checkpoint frequency trades latency vs. cost (ack overhead). Conservative default: checkpoint every 512 tokens OR when session.checkpoint called explicitly.
- Tool invocations carry separate cost units; SDK will expose estimated cost hints and allow preemptive aborts when budget is close.

Observable signals and telemetry (high level)
- Metrics to emit: checkpoint_latency_p50/95, microresponse_rate, tool_invoke_latency, tool_replay_count, session_resume_success_rate, budget_exceeded_count.
- Structured logs: checkpoint lifecycle events, tool token issuance/replay, resume reconciliation traces. These feed Redwood Console rollups.

Compatibility & migration notes
- Backwards compatible: clients that ignore the Conductor keep receiving raw microresponse frames. Conductor opt-in when app instantiates session via conductor.startSession.
- Migration path: incremental rollouts by route; server will advertise conductor-friendly frames via capability bit in handshake.

Security & compliance concerns
- Tool tokens are authorized tokens tied to session; need short TTL and rotation.
- Checkpoint acknowledgements may reference PII if tool outputs include extracted data — ensure KMS/HSM controls when persisting in Private deployments.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should checkpoint acknowledgements be strictly ordered? (pros: simpler resume semantics; cons: potential head-of-line blocking).
- How aggressively should SDK garbage-collect local state? (policy knobs needed)
- Expose a debug mode that opens a deterministic replay log for test harnesses — what retention policy?
- Mobile offline: we need a safe fallback for very long offline windows where server token TTL expires. Offer local-only queue with eventual reconciliation?
- Can we unify commit semantics across Dedicated and Private deployments with differing compliance constraints?

Rollout plan (rough)
- Phase 0 (labs): SDK experiment in JS only, server supports tool_token echo and checkpoint_hint (2 sprints).
- Phase 1 (canary): opt-in rollout for a small percent of hosted-api traffic and internal feature flags; collect telemetry and test resume cases (2 months).
- Phase 2: SDK parity for mobile (iOS/Android), migration guide for customers, console dashboards for checkpoint telemetry (3 months).

Backward compatibility tests and playbooks
- Repeat receives with same seq/checkpoint must not double-commit. Test harness: flaky network emitter that replays frames out-of-order.
- Tool replay idempotency test that intentionally replays with modified args - ensure server rejects divergent replays with clear error codes.

Example flow (narrative)
1) App calls conductor.startSession('/compose', { userId }, { latency_budget_ms: 600, commit_mode: 'auto' }).
2) Server sends small microresponses while an OCR tool runs in parallel. App displays partial text updates and starts a ToolResultStream for OCR.
3) App calls session.checkpoint('paragraph-1'). SDK persists checkpoint locally and awaits server ack.
4) On poor network, client disconnects after emitting checkpoint locally. On reconnect, session.resumeFrom('paragraph-1') re-fetches server map, sees tool_token pending, replays the invocation using same token; server returns a toolEvent that is idempotent.
5) Once checkpoint acked, the Conductor marks associated tool outputs committed and emits session.on('commit', { checkpoint: 'paragraph-1' }).

Implementation notes (engineering constraints)
- Keep the client runtime tiny: shared JS runtime with an optional TypeScript types package. Mobile implementations should aim to reuse core invariants, but native storage adapters will be required.
- Server needs a small lightweight store mapping session -> checkpoint hints -> outstanding tool tokens to support resume. This can be bounded TTL.

Next steps (immediate)
- Align with serving-runtime and infra on minimal protocol changes (seq, checkpoint_hint, tool_token) — schedule an syncto next week.
- Prototype JS SDK conductor.startSession + simple checkpoint roundtrip in a spike. Owner: Ethan Morales.
- Draft protocol PR and toy server shim for replay idempotency tests. Owner: Marcus Liu.

Notes to self (scratch)
- Keep wording accessible: customers must be able to opt-out; we must not force new semantics onto older clients.
- Hunting for sweet spot on checkpoint defaults — aim for 3–5 checkpoints per average short conversation.
- Add concrete examples in PRD later: code snippets for web, iOS.

Referenced tickets/threads
- Linear: INF-3423 (Handshake conductor spike)
- Slack: #hosted-api-tooling thread on disconnect-resume patterns (thread-PLQ9w2Zx)
- GH: hosted-sdk PR #719 - initial conductor prototype

Acknowledgements
Thanks to Rhea for early UX sketches and Marcus for spike infra notes.
